newsitem.title: USA: AT&T finance chief to leave at end of March.
newsitem.headline: AT&T finance chief to leave at end of March.

text.p: AT&T Corp.'s chief financial officer plans to leave the company at the end of March, AT&T said Monday.
Richard Miller, 56, plans to pursue interests outside the telecommunications industry, following through on plans he made a year ago, AT&T said.

Miller is one of a number of senior executives to leave AT&T in the last six months, but the company emphasised his departure was not inspired by other opportunities in the industry or as a result of changes by AT&T itself.
Miller said in an interview that he told AT&T Robert Allen a year ago in a letter that he wanted to leave.
"Basically in that letter I said that when we complete the restructuring, the company will be a very different one to the one I joined," Miller said.

AT&T on Dec. 31 completed its split into three parts: a telecommunications firm, equipment maker Lucent Technologies Inc. and computer firm NCR Corp. It also sold its AT&T Capital Corp. finance unit as part of the restructuring.
Miller said there were several strong internal candidates to replace him, but that Allen and John Walter, who in October was named chief operating officer, would also look outside the company.
Miller joined AT&T as chief financial officer in August 1993.
